names.name: Oklahoma Track (first meet)
names.operator: John Morrissey
names.note: First thoroughbred card 3 Aug 1863 on the Oklahoma Track, across the street from the present course

names.name: Saratoga Race Course
names.operator: Morrissey and partners; Gottfried Waldbaum (1892); W. C. Whitney investor group (1901); New York Racing Association (current)
names.note: Morrissey built the new course and grandstand across the street in 1864; closed 1896 and 1911-12 (anti-gambling law), curtailed 1943-45

label.basis: Kefauver Part 7 treats Saratoga lake houses (Arrowhead Inn, Piping Rock), and a text search of that volume finds neither the Race Course nor Morrissey; no source opened ties the track to organised crime.

venues.corrections: None needed on dates. The label "none" holds, but the hearings did involve Saratoga Springs gambling at other venues (the lake houses); the summary could say so.

names.name: Saratoga Clubhouse
names.operator: John Morrissey (1866-1878); Albert Spencer and Charles Reed (after 1878)
names.note: Gambling clubhouse begun 1866; main building 1870

names.name: Canfield Casino (Saratoga Clubhouse under Canfield)
names.operator: Richard A. Canfield
names.note: Canfield partner 1893, owner 1894; added dining wing 1902-03; gambling banned by reformers 1907; sold to the city 1911

names.name: Canfield Casino (museum)
names.operator: City of Saratoga Springs
names.note: Buildings house the Saratoga Springs History Museum; not demolished

label.basis: Gambling ended in 1907, decades before the Kefauver era; the Saratoga mob-era gambling in the opened sources was at the lake houses, not here.

venues.corrections: Opening: gambling at the site began 1866 as the Saratoga Clubhouse; 1870 is the date of the main building. Closing 1907 is for gambling only; the building survives as a museum. Summary correct that it predates organised crime.

names.name: Canterbury Downs
names.operator: Minnesota Racetrack Inc. (Walter Brooks Fields Jr. and investors; Santa Anita partner)
names.note: First race 26 Jun 1985

names.name: New Canterbury Downs
names.operator: Ladbroke Racing Corporation
names.note: Sold 1990; closed Dec 1992 after a poor season

names.name: Canterbury Park
names.operator: Curtis and Randy Sampson (after Irwin L. Jacobs, late 1993)
names.note: Live racing returned late 1994; renamed Jan 1995; card room 1999

label.basis: Page describes a track and card room regulated by the Minnesota Racing Commission; no allegation on it or in a dedicated search; Commission records not opened.

venues.corrections: "closed" null is fine for today but the track was closed for racing Dec 1992 to 1994. Summary "no organized crime ties" is supported only by absence of reports.

names.name: Grand Casino Mille Lacs
names.operator: Grand Casinos Inc. (management, early 1990s; bought by Hilton 1998 to form Park Place Entertainment); Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe (owner and operator)
names.note: Opened early 1990s; the year 1991 is not confirmed by an opened page; hand-over of management not dated by an opened source

label.basis: No allegation found in the pages opened or in a dedicated search; only general congressional statements on Indian gaming, which name no venue.

venues.corrections: None established. Opening year 1991 unconfirmed (sources say "early 1990s").

names.name: Foxwoods (high-stakes bingo hall)
names.operator: Mashantucket Pequot Tribe
names.note: Founded 1986 as a bingo hall

names.name: Foxwoods Resort Casino
names.operator: Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation
names.note: Table games 1992, slots 1993; Grand Pequot Tower 1997

names.name: MGM Grand at Foxwoods / Fox Tower
names.operator: Tribe, with MGM Mirage as brand partner to 2013
names.note: Separate tower opened 17 May 2008; renamed Fox Tower 2013

label.basis: A 1996 wire report says authorities were focusing on associates of a crime family over a cheating scheme involving dealers and patrons at the casino; the tribe reported it and says it banned 52 people for such associations; no charge against the tribe or its government appears.

venues.corrections: "No organized crime involvement" is too strong: a 1996 report links a scheme at the casino to associates of a crime family. The casino and tribe are described as the party that detected and reported it. The casino began as bingo in 1986; 1992 is the start of table games.

names.name: Little Six Bingo
names.operator: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community
names.note: Precursor on the reservation

names.name: Little Six Casino
names.operator: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community
names.note: Became a casino after the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act and state compact; still operated

names.name: Mystic Lake Casino Hotel
names.operator: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community
names.note: Opened 12 May 1992

label.basis: No allegation in the pages opened or a dedicated search; only general statements on Indian gaming.

names.name: Turning Stone Resort Casino
names.operator: Oneida Indian Nation of New York
names.note: Opened 20 Jul 1993; hotel 1994-96; compact and land disputes with the state resolved 2013

label.basis: The legal disputes on the page concern the compact and land, not crime; a mob-contractor search found nothing; general testimony says no substantial infiltration of Indian gaming.

names.name: Mohegan Sun
names.operator: Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority (1995); Trading Cove Associates (developer-manager: Sun International/Kerzner 50%, Waterford Gaming 50%) with 5% of gross revenue to 2014
names.note: Opened 12 Oct 1996; page says control passed to the tribe in 2000 (not independently checked)

label.basis: Searches returned only cheating cases involving patrons and dealers; no source opened ties ownership or development to organised crime.

venues.corrections: None on dates. The 2000 date for the hand-over of control is a Wikipedia statement to be checked.

names.name: MGM Grand Detroit (temporary casino)
names.operator: MGM Grand Inc, later MGM Mirage
names.note: Opened 29 Jul 1999 in a converted IRS office; first legal casino in Detroit

names.name: MGM Grand Detroit (permanent resort)
names.operator: MGM Resorts International (operator); Vici Properties (real estate)
names.note: Opened 3 Oct 2007; 2005 merger forced MGM to choose between this and MotorCity

label.basis: No finding against the operator; a 1999 report raised background concerns about the landlord of the temporary building, who denied wrongdoing.

venues.corrections: "No organized crime ties" is supported for the operator, but in 1999 the press reported background concerns about the landlord of the temporary building, who denied wrongdoing.

names.name: MotorCity Casino
names.operator: Mandalay Resort Group (53.5%); Marian Ilitch (25%)
names.note: Opened 14 Dec 1999

names.name: MotorCity Casino Hotel
names.operator: Marian Ilitch
names.note: Ilitch bought the Mandalay stake 12 Apr 2005 for $525 million after the MGM Mirage-Mandalay merger

label.basis: No source opened alleges organised-crime ties; Wikipedia only for the ownership thread.

venues.corrections: "Developed by Marian Ilitch" is imprecise: it opened under Mandalay as majority owner, and Ilitch took control in 2005.

names.name: Greektown Casino
names.operator: Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians (90% after buy-out; Millennium Management managed to 2002)
names.note: Opened 10 Nov 2000; Chapter 11 May 2008

names.name: Greektown Casino (Superholdings)
names.operator: Greektown Superholdings, Inc. (bondholders)
names.note: Bought out of bankruptcy June 2010

names.name: Greektown Casino
names.operator: Rock Gaming (Dan Gilbert), later Jack Entertainment
names.note: Majority stake Jan 2013; planned rename Jack Detroit Casino-Hotel Greektown announced 2016, cancelled 2018

names.name: Hollywood Casino at Greektown
names.operator: Penn Entertainment (operator); Vici Properties (real estate)
names.note: Penn and Vici bought it May 2019; rebranded Hollywood Casino May 2022

label.basis: State background checks raised concerns about two minority-owner couples, forcing a buy-out; the sources opened do not say organised crime.

venues.corrections: Record says "opened ... by the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe ... later sold to Penn": the sale was in stages (bankruptcy 2010, Rock Gaming 2013, Penn/Vici 2019). Nature of the 2000 concerns about the minority owners is not given by any page opened.

names.name: Pechanga Resort & Casino
names.operator: Pechanga Band of Luiseno Indians (tribe now styles itself Pechanga Band of Indians)
names.note: Opened 24 Jun 2002; expanded 2004 and 2018

label.basis: No allegation in the page opened or a dedicated search; only general statements on Indian gaming.

gaps: Grand Casino Mille Lacs: Wikipedia page for the venue returned a rate-limit error four times; the 1991 opening year and the date the Band took over management are unconfirmed. Recalled, not fetched: April 1991 opening (from search snippets only).

michigan.gov (Michigan Gaming Control Board), justice.gov, senate.gov, nigc.gov, mlbo.dev, web.archive.org and themobmuseum.org refused through the proxy, so no Gaming Control Board order on the 2000 Greektown buy-out or on MGM Grand/MotorCity suitability was read.

Detroit venues (MGM Grand, MotorCity, Greektown) rest on Wikipedia and two Las Vegas Sun wire reports; no court record or board finding opened. Labels 'none' mean no credible tie was found, not that suitability files were read.

Tribal venues (Mille Lacs, Mystic Lake, Turning Stone, Mohegan, Pechanga) have no venue-specific primary source; the congressional statements are general. Tribal gaming commission and NIGC records not opened.
Foxwoods 1996: no later court record or outcome of the state police investigation was opened.
Canterbury Park: Minnesota Racing Commission records not opened.
